Plot the edge betweenness of an htna network

Source: R/edge_betweenness.R
plot_edge_betweenness_htna.Rd

plot_edge_betweenness_htna() plots the edge-betweenness network of an htna network: each transition is drawn with a width given by the number of shortest paths that pass through it, in the layout and actor styling of plot_htna(). The widest edges are the bridges of the interaction, the transitions through which the flow between the codes of the actors is channeled.

plot_edge_betweenness_htna() computes the scores with edge_betweenness_htna() (unless x already holds them) and draws all edges with a non-zero score, unless minimum is given. It is called for the plot and returns, invisibly, the value of plot_htna().

Usage

plot_edge_betweenness_htna(x, directed = TRUE, invert = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna network, or a result of edge_betweenness_htna().

directed, invert

Passed to edge_betweenness_htna() when x is an htna network; ignored otherwise. Defaults TRUE.

...

Further arguments of plot_htna(), such as minimum, layout or group_colors.

Value

Called for the plot. Invisibly, the value of plot_htna().

Conditions

htna_bad_input when x is not an htna network.

See also

edge_betweenness_htna(), plot_htna()

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
plot_edge_betweenness_htna(net)

plot_edge_betweenness_htna(net, minimum = 5)
